newsitem.title: ITALY: Fed not seen raising rates after election - Angell [CORRECTED 17:19 GMT].
newsitem.headline: Fed not seen raising rates after election - Angell [CORRECTED 17:19 GMT].

text.p: The Federal Reserve is very unlikely to raise interest rates at the next meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) on November 13, said Wayne Angell, former Federal Reserve Board Governor.
(Corrects Angell's title from former governor of the Kansas City Federal Reserve Bank).

"Unless there is surprising data on the inflation front the Fed will not decide an increase in interest rates immediately after the (presidential) election," said Angell, now chief economist at Bear Stearns, at a conference on Friday.
The U.S. presidential election is November 5.
A movement in interest rates next month would give the impression that monetary policy is subordinated to the electoral cycle, Angell said.
"The Fed must continue to pursue the objective of controlling inflation without waiting for a recession to put a break on price growth," he said.
"The Fed will sustain growth if it pursues its anti-inflation objective without worrying about repercussions on employment."

Angell said he expected U.S. GDP to grow at 2.75 percent in the second half of 1996 and a gradual slowdown in the months after that. He predicted 1997 first half growth of 2.5 percent, slowing down to 2.25 percent in the second half of next year.
